articles.title: Insumos da natureza | G1
articles.standfirst: Bioinsumos ganham espaço na agricultura e ampliam alternativas para o desenvolvimento das lavouras.
articles.summary: Bioinsumos ganham espaço na agricultura e ampliam alternativas para o desenvolvimento das lavouras.
articles.body:
A evolução da agricultura ao longo dos anos é marcada pelo uso de novas tecnologias, desde máquinas de colheita até inteligência artificial e satélites para a otimização da produção. A atualização tende a facilitar o trabalho no campo e contribuir para uma produção mais eficiente. No segundo trimestre de 2026, o Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) brasileiro cresceu 0,5% em relação ao trimestre anterior, enquanto o setor agropecuário segue entre os segmentos que movimentam a economia nacional.

A sustentabilidade é um dos pilares quando a intenção é manter o crescimento e o desenvolvimento alinhados à conservação do meio ambiente. Nesse cenário, os bioinsumos vêm ganhando espaço na agricultura brasileira. Dados do CropData, da CropLife Brasil, apontam que 46 milhões de hectares foram tratados com bioinsumos no primeiro semestre de 2026, alta de 18,3% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. No período, o mercado movimentou R$1,8 bilhão.

A análise de microrganismos faz parte do processo de desenvolvimento de bioinsumos. — Foto: Divulgação/Milena Rolim.

Mas qual é a diferença deles para os insumos convencionais?

Os bioinsumos são produzidos a partir de agentes de origem biológica, como fungos, bactérias e outros microrganismos, que podem atuar na proteção, no desenvolvimento e no manejo das lavouras. No Brasil, o Programa Nacional de Bioinsumos foi criado em 2020, por meio do Decreto nº 10.375, com o objetivo de ampliar e fortalecer a utilizaICITIESção dessas tecnologias na agropecuária.

A legislação brasileira também passou a contar com um marco regulatório específico para o setor. A Lei nº 15.070, de 23 de dezembro de 2024, estabelece que bioinsumos são produtos, processos ou tecnologias de origem vegetal, animal ou microbiana, inclusive aqueles obtidos por processos biotecnológicos, destinados a diferentes aplicações na produção agropecuária.

Eles podem ser utilizados na produção, proteção, armazenamento e beneficiamento de produtos agropecuários, além de contribuir para o crescimento e desenvolvimento de plantas e para diferentes processos biológicos relacionados à produção.

Microrganismos presentes na natureza também podem ter aplicações na agricultura. — Foto: Divulgação/Milena Rolim.

O conceito de sustentabilidade está relacionado à capacidade de suprir as necessidades do presente sem comprometer a capacidade das gerações futuras de satisfazerem suas próprias necessidades. Na agricultura, esse princípio coloca em discussão a busca por produtividade aliada à conservação dos recursos naturais.

Os bioinsumos aparecem como uma das alternativas nesse cenário. O uso de produtos biológicos pode ser integrado a outras estratégias de manejo, inclusive em conjunto com produtos químicos, ampliando as ferramentas disponíveis ao produtor para o controle de pragas e doenças.

Segundo a CropLife Brasil, essa combinação faz parte do manejo integrado de pragas e tem contribuído para a expansão do uso dos produtos biológicos no campo. No primeiro semestre de 2026, os bioinseticidas representaram 47% do valor das vendas de bioinsumos no país, com cerca de R$858 milhões movimentados e 16,4 milhões de hectares tratados.

A pesquisa busca novas aplicações para os microrganismos. — Foto: Divulgação/Milena Rolim.

A popularização gradativa dessas tecnologias acompanha uma transformação no setor agrícola, que também envolve o uso de inteligência artificial, automação, drones, satélites e melhoramento genético. Nesse contexto, os bioinsumos representam mais uma possibilidade para o produtor buscar eficiência no manejo das lavouras.

O crescimento do setor também está relacionado à busca por práticas agrícolas mais sustentáveis. Em 2025, o mercado brasileiro de bioinsumos movimentou R$6,2 bilhões, crescimento de 15% em relação ao ano anterior. A área tratada chegou a 194 milhões de hectares, alta de 28%.

Com a expansão do uso dessas tecnologias, os bioinsumos passam a ocupar um espaço cada vez maior nas discussões sobre o futuro da agricultura. A combinação entre inovação, produtividade e conservação dos recursos naturais apresenta novos caminhos para o desenvolvimento do setor.

Texto produzido por Luis Figueiredo, acadêmico do curso de Jornalismo do Centro Universitário FAG, sob orientação da professora Julliane Brita, para a 24ª edição da Revista Verbo, veiculada na 5ª edição do City Farm FAG.

articles.title: Apartamentos compactos em Mogi das Cruzes: tendência para morar e investir | G1
articles.standfirst: Imóveis de até 66 m² combinam localização estratégica, áreas de lazer completas e soluções modernas para quem busca economia e praticidade
articles.summary: Imóveis de até 66 m² combinam localização estratégica, áreas de lazer completas e soluções modernas para quem busca economia e praticidade
articles.body:
Apartamento de 47 m2 do Máximo Braz Cubas, em Mogi das Cruzes — Foto: Divulgação

Os apartamentos compactos ganham cada vez mais espaço no mercado imobiliário, com participação expressiva nos lançamentos das cidades paulistas analisadas em pesquisas recentes do Secovi-SP, sindicato do setor. A procura por imóveis pequenos reflete mudanças no comportamento do consumidor, que hoje valoriza localização, praticidade, economia e potencial de geração de renda.

Esses imóveis se tornam ainda mais práticos quando estão localizados em bairros bem estruturados, perto do trabalho e de facilidades como transporte público, comércio, gastronomia e serviços. Afinal, ganhar tempo é essencial na vida moderna.

Economia: do valor de compra ao custo de vida

Os compactos, em geral, têm valor mais acessível e condições de financiamento facilitadas, podendo atender, inclusive, famílias enquadradas no programa Minha Casa, Minha Vida. Além disso, proporcionam economia com mobiliário, decoração, limpeza, manutenção, condomínio e IPTU.

Não por acaso, o segmento chama a atenção dos investidores, devido à demanda por locação tradicional e de curta temporada. São imóveis que atraem jovens profissionais, pessoas que moram sozinhas, casais, estudantes e trabalhadores com residência em outra cidade.

Hoje quem mora em um compacto economiza até na hora de receber os amigos, aproveitar momentos de lazer e realizar pequenos reparos. Isso porque os condomínios modernos oferecem áreas gourmet, churrasqueiras, pet places para a diversão de cães e gatos e até espaços com ferramentas compartilhadas.

Casa de campo, com piscina privativa, do Máximo Braz Cubas — Foto: Divulgação

As áreas de lazer do Soma Galeria e do Máximo Braz Cubas, em Mogi das Cruzes, são tão completas que têm até casa de campo, um espaço especial dentro do condomínio, com churrasqueira e uma piscina privativa que pode ser utilizada pelos convidados dos moradores durante o evento.

Apartamentos compactos da Ribeira em Mogi

O Soma já está pronto para morar e fica no Parque Galeria, um bairro do Mogilar planejado para reunir moradia, comércio, serviços e áreas de convivência, além de estar situado bem perto da estação Estudantes da CPTM. Já o Máximo é o mais novo lançamento da Ribeira Empreendimentos Imobiliários, ao lado da estação Braz Cubas.

Os dois proporcionam ótima mobilidade, e seus moradores podem chegar com muita facilidade à capital paulista. Outros empreendimentos de Braz Cubas são o Happy e o Total, também prontos para morar, permitindo que os proprietários façam sua mudança imediatamente ou coloquem o imóvel para alugar.

O Soma, o Máximo, o Happy e o Total inauguram um novo jeito de morar em Mogi das Cruzes. Os apartamentos variam de 33 a 66 m², com 1, 2 ou 3 dormitórios, dependendo do condomínio. Todos estão localizados em regiões com muitas opções de comércio, serviços e educação. O Soma, inclusive, fica perto das universidades Mogi das Cruzes e Braz Cubas, atraindo estudantes em busca de moradia.

Robô que leva as encomendas da portaria aos apartamentos do Máximo Braz Cubas — Foto: Divulgação

Todos têm soluções inteligentes que facilitam a vida dos moradores, como espaço delivery com refrigerador para guardar encomendas. O Máximo ainda tem um robô que leva as entregas da portaria até o apartamento. O Máximo e o Soma disponibilizam bicicletas e patinetes elétricos compartilhados entre os moradores.

Outro grande diferencial dos empreendimentos da Ribeira é que os apartamentos já são entregues com piso instalado, evitando desperdício e gastos extras com reformas.

Patinetes compartilhados entre os moradores do Soma Galeria — Foto: Divulgação

Com opções para diferentes perfis e estilos de vida, os condomínios da Ribeira mostram que é possível unir conforto, praticidade e potencial de investimento em Mogi das Cruzes.

É possível visitar os decorados dos condomínios de Braz Cubas no estande da Ribeira, situado ao lado da Simpar, também conhecida como Julio Simões: Av. Francisco Ferreira Lopes, 3.474, Mogi das Cruzes.

articles.title: Em 15 dias, chove menos de 20% do previsto para outubro em Rio Branco | G1
articles.standfirst: Se consideradas as chuvas registradas até domingo (18), percentual sobe para 39,2%, mas ainda insuficiente para alcançar os 150 mm previstos pela Defesa Civil Municipal para o mês.
articles.summary: Se consideradas as chuvas registradas até domingo (18), percentual sobe para 39,2%, mas ainda insuficiente para alcançar os 150 mm previstos pela Defesa Civil Municipal para o mês.
articles.body:
Rio Branco registrou cerca de 27,66 milímetros (mm) nos primeiros 15 dias de outubro . Isto é o que aponta o levantamento divulgado pela Defesa Civil municipal. O volume representa 18,4% do previsto para todo o mês, que é de 150 mm.

Se considerado até domingo (18), o número sobe para 58,86 mm , ou 39,2% do total. A influência desta subida deve-se às fortes chuvas da última sexta (16) , quando foram registrados cerca de 25 mm em duas horas. O fenômeno alagou ruas e trouxe outras consequências. ( Assista ao vídeo acima )

Ao g1 , o coordenador da Defesa Civil municipal, tenente-coronel Cláudio Falcão, disse que a expectativa é que o volume de chuva na segunda quinzena fique próximo ao que foi registrado nos primeiros 15 dias do mês .

Para alcançar o volume de 150 mm até o fim de outubro, ainda seriam necessários cerca de 91,14 mm.

"Possivelmente, a gente deve repetir agora na segunda quinzena, caso não haja nada fora da curva. Mesmo dessa maneira, a gente não consegue alcançar o que é esperado para o mês", afirmou o coordenador.

Os registros referentes a 1º e 18 de outubro apontam que a chuva ocorreu em cinco dias do mês , com maior concentração na sexta, que teve mais da metade do volume acumulado na primeira quinzena. Confira abaixo:

Rio Branco registrou 58,86 mm de chuva até o dia 18 desse mês — Foto: Arquivo/Defesa Civil de Rio Branco

A previsão do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) para segunda-feira (19) indica a continuidade das condições de instabilidade no estado acreano, com pancadas de chuva e trovoadas isoladas.

O instituto ainda mantém aviso amarelo de perigo potencial para tempestades no Acre e em áreas de estados vizinhos.

O alerta indica possibilidade de condições meteorológicas adversas, mas não significa que tempestades intensas ocorram em todos os municípios acreanos.

No temporal, de sexta, a Unidade de Saúde da Família (USF) Gentil Perdomo , no Conjunto Esperança, ficou alagada após a forte chuva. Além disso, também foram afetadas as Uraps Roney Meireles e Vila Ivonete, além da USF Raimunda Dionísio, Sebastiana Prado, todas na capital.

articles.title: 11 de setembro: Suprema Corte dos EUA nega recurso de mentor | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão mantém o julgamento militar dos quatro acusados pelos ataques que mataram cerca de 3 mil pessoas em 2001, previsto para começar em junho de 2028, em Guantánamo.
articles.summary: 11 de setembro: Suprema Corte dos EUA mantém julgamento militar de Khalid Sheikh Mohammed em Guantánamo, previsto para começar em junho de 2028.
articles.body:
Foto de arquivo: Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, suposto mentor dos ataques de 11 de Setembro, é visto logo após sua captura durante uma operação de invasão no Paquistão, em 1º de março de 2003 — Foto: AP, Arquivo

A Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos rejeitou, nesta segunda-feira (19), um recurso de Khalid Sheikh Mohammed , considerado o mentor dos atentados de 11 de setembro de 2001 contra o World Trade Center , e de dois outros participantes do plano, que buscava restabelecer seu acordo de culpabilidade, que foi anulado em 2025.

A Corte rejeitou o recurso, que cancelaria a realização de seu julgamento perante um tribunal militar em Guantánamo , previsto a partir de junho de 2028.

Mohammed e outros três acusados (Walid ben Attash, Mustafa al-Hawsawi e Ammar al Baluchi, também conhecido como Ali Abdul Aziz Ali) serão julgados por terrorismo e pela morte de cerca de 3.000 pessoas nos atentados em Nova York .

Paquistanês criado no Kuwait, Mohammed foi um dos principais tenentes de Osama bin Laden dentro da organização jihadista Al-Qaeda até sua captura em março de 2003, no Paquistão.

Os quatro homens, que estão entre os últimos detidos na base militar americana de Guantánamo, em Cuba, nunca foram julgados, já que o processo se estagnou para determinar se as torturas sofridas invalidariam as provas de acusação reunidas contra eles .

A Justiça Militar americana declarou em agosto inadmissíveis as confissões de Mohammed, que passou por prisões secretas da CIA na Polônia, onde sofreu sessões de interrogatório sob tortura antes de sua transferência para Guantánamo em setembro de 2006, incluindo suas declarações a interrogadores na base militar em 2007.

Em julho de 2025, um tribunal de apelação americano havia anulado o acordo de culpabilidade firmado por Mohammed e dois partícipes, atrasando ainda mais a resolução judicial de um dos episódios mais traumáticos da história dos Estados Unidos .

Esses acordos, que sem dúvida lhes teriam evitado enfrentar a pena de morte, geraram polêmica em plena campanha para as eleições presidenciais de novembro de 2024.

Khalid Sheikh Mohammed nasceu no Kuwait e se formou em engenharia mecânica nos Estados Unidos . Ligado à Al-Qaeda de Osama bin Laden , foi preso no Paquistão em 2003 e passou anos em prisões secretas da CIA antes de ser transferido para Guantánamo, onde permanece detido à espera de julgamento.

Khalid nasceu em uma família de origem balúchi. Aos 16 anos, aderiu ao jihadismo. Em 1983, mudou-se para os Estados Unidos para estudar e se formou em engenharia mecânica em 1986.

🔎 O jihadismo é uma corrente extremista do Islã que defende o uso da violência armada em nome de uma interpretação radical do conceito islâmico de jihad, que pode ser traduzido como “guerra santa”. O termo é usado para descrever grupos que buscam criar sociedades ou Estados baseados em sua interpretação rígida da religião. Organizações como Al-Qaeda, o Estado Islâmico, o Talibã, o Hezzbollah e o Hamas são exemplos de grupos jihadistas.

No ano seguinte, foi ao Paquistão e se juntou a combatentes jihadistas que lutavam contra as tropas soviéticas no Afeganistão.

Na década de 1990, Mohammed aproximou-se de grupos extremistas e manteve contatos com militantes envolvidos em conspirações contra os Estados Unidos .

Em 1996, apresentou a Osama bin Laden , fundador da Al-Qaeda, um plano para sequestrar aviões comerciais e lançá-los contra edifícios importantes em território americano.

Inicialmente considerado complexo demais, o projeto foi reformulado e acabou aprovado por bin Laden entre o fim de 1998 e o início de 1999.

articles.title: Tecnologia organiza a gestão do investimento em short stay | G1
articles.standfirst: Anúncios, reservas, preços e atendimento podem ser integrados para apoiar a operação e o acompanhamento pelo investidor.
articles.summary: Anúncios, reservas, preços e atendimento podem ser integrados para apoiar a operação e o acompanhamento pelo investidor.
articles.body:
A tecnologia organiza a gestão do investimento em short stay ao reunir informações e tarefas de cada estadia. Divulgar a unidade, responder interessados, atualizar a disponibilidade e preparar o apartamento para a próxima chegada são etapas que precisam funcionar de forma coordenada.

Plataformas especializadas podem apoiar esse processo e dar ao proprietário uma visão mais clara das reservas e do movimento do imóvel.

No Compass109, empreendimento de investimento em short stay desenvolvido pela Dancon em Londrina, a parceria com a Housi integra a proposta de gestão profissional, conforme o escopo contratado.

Divulgação e reservas em uma operação integrada

A jornada começa quando uma pessoa procura uma acomodação. Fotografias, descrição da unidade, informações sobre o edifício e disponibilidade ajudam o interessado a escolher.

Uma gestão integrada organiza a presença do imóvel em diferentes canais e concentra o acompanhamento das reservas. A sincronização dos calendários permite atualizar a disponibilidade quando uma estadia é confirmada.

Para o investidor, a proposta é acompanhar informações que, em uma operação individual, poderiam ficar distribuídas entre anúncios, mensagens e controles separados.

A procura por acomodações pode mudar entre dias úteis, fins de semana, feriados e períodos com grandes eventos.

Ferramentas de precificação apoiam ajustes nas diárias conforme a demanda e as características da unidade. Esses recursos podem orientar decisões, mas não asseguram que uma reserva será realizada pelo preço anunciado.

O acompanhamento deve considerar o equilíbrio entre valor da diária e ocupação. Uma diária maior, isoladamente, não significa uma receita mensal maior.

Depois da reserva, o hóspede precisa receber orientações sobre endereço, horários e acesso. Durante a estadia, pode precisar de atendimento ou de informações sobre a unidade.

Ao final da permanência, começa a preparação para a próxima reserva. Limpeza, troca de enxoval e vistoria precisam ser coordenadas dentro do intervalo disponível.

A integração dessas etapas facilita a comunicação com os prestadores envolvidos e a organização do intervalo entre as reservas. A regularidade do serviço é parte da oferta de estadia.

Nos serviços previstos pela Housi, essas atividades poderão compor a gestão, de acordo com o escopo contratado.

Dados para acompanhar receitas e despesas

Para o investidor, o acompanhamento deve reunir reservas, receitas, despesas e repasses. O valor recebido pelas estadias precisa ser analisado junto aos custos de manter a unidade disponível.

Relatórios ajudam a observar períodos com maior procura, custos recorrentes e necessidades de manutenção. A análise ao longo do tempo permite comparar o desempenho efetivo com as premissas do investimento.

O atendimento humano complementa as ferramentas digitais quando surgem dúvidas ou situações que exigem uma solução específica durante a estadia.

Como a proposta se conecta ao Compass109

O Compass109 reúne diferentes plantas e áreas compartilhadas para compor uma oferta de locações temporárias. A estrutura física e a operação precisam ser consideradas em conjunto pelo investidor.

A parceria com a Housi acrescenta ao projeto a proposta de gestão profissional do short stay. O investidor deverá avaliar os serviços disponíveis, as taxas e os critérios para disponibilizar sua unidade.

O alcance da gestão e as responsabilidades serão definidos nos contratos aplicáveis. A organização operacional apoia a administração, mas o resultado continua sujeito à demanda, à vacância e às despesas do imóvel.

Ao concentrar etapas e informações, a tecnologia oferece uma forma de acompanhar o investimento, da divulgação ao repasse dos valores das estadias.

articles.title: T-Pain sues Akon's record label over nearly $500,000 in allegedly unpaid royalties; it's his second lawsuit against the company
articles.summary: American rapper and singer T-Pain has filed a second lawsuit against Konvict Entertainment, the record label co-founded by singer Akon, alleging that it
articles.body: American rapper and singer T-Pain has filed a second lawsuit against Konvict Entertainment, the record label co-founded by singer Akon, alleging that it owes him $489,047.76 in unpaid royalties. Filed in Fulton County Superior Court in Georgia on September 4, 2026, the lawsuit concerns royalties from music sales during the second half of 2025. T-Pain, whose legal name is Faheem Rashad Najm, claims the company failed to pay him the full amount due under his 2005 recording agreement and a settlement reached in 2025 to resolve an earlier legal dispute. The new case follows a royalty payment of more than $1.3 million that Konvict allegedly received from distributor Zomba Recordings in March. T-Pain is seeking the outstanding amount, along with interest and legal fees.T-Pain claims Konvict owes him nearly $500,000According to the lawsuit, Konvict Entertainment received $1,304,127 from Zomba Recordings on March 30, 2026, for sales during the second half of 2025. T-Pain alleges that his recording agreement entitles him to 75% of the net royalties Konvict receives from distributors for his recordings.The complaint says Konvict paid T-Pain $489,047 in early June but failed to pay a further $489,047.76 that he claims is owed. He alleges that the company did not resolve the matter despite receiving written notice.The lawsuit seeks the outstanding royalties, prejudgment interest and attorney fees. The amount remains disputed and has not been established by a court.Dispute follows a 2025 settlementThe latest case revives a dispute that began in 2018, when T-Pain sued Konvict Entertainment over alleged payment failures connected to his fifth studio album, Oblivion. The earlier lawsuit included claims involving an unpaid advance, payment due upon delivery of the album and royalties under his recording agreement.Konvict denied liability in that case. Following years of mediation, the parties reached a settlement in 2025 under which the label agreed to pay T-Pain $114,000. According to reporting by The Atlanta Journal-Constitution, the settlement covered royalties collected through the end of 2024.In the new complaint, T-Pain alleges that Konvict breached both the original recording agreement and the 2025 settlement by failing to pay the royalties at issue. The latest claim concerns a later period of music sales than the royalties covered by the earlier settlement.Why BuVision features in the lawsuitT-Pain's complaint alleges that Konvict directed his representatives to seek the outstanding payment from BuVision, an affiliate associated with Abou “Bu” Thiam, Akon's younger brother. According to the complaint, attempts to contact BuVision about the remaining amount were unsuccessful.BuVision and Thiam are not named as defendants in the new case. Konvict Entertainment is the sole defendant, and the claim concerns its alleged failure to fulfil its contractual payment obligations.T-Pain and Akon have a long musical historyT-Pain signed with Konvict Entertainment in 2005, a period that helped establish his recording career. He later collaborated with Akon, co-writing “I Can't Wait” and “Holla Holla” for Akon's 2006 album Konvicted. Akon also featured on T-Pain's 2007 song “Bartender”, from the album Epiphany.Although Akon co-founded Konvict Entertainment, he is not listed as a defendant in the new lawsuit. The case is directed at the record label over the alleged unpaid royalties.When The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported the lawsuit on September 8, 2026, it said Konvict Entertainment and T-Pain's lawyers had not responded to its requests for comment. The label had denied liability in the earlier case before agreeing to the 2025 settlement.The new lawsuit seeks to determine whether Konvict failed to pay the amount T-Pain claims is due under the recording agreement and settlement. The allegations remain unresolved in court.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: 32-year-old Kavan Patel, an Indian-origin store owner in Florida's West Melbourne, has been charged with murder after a 14-year-old boy on his bike, who
articles.body: 32-year-old Kavan Patel, an Indian-origin store owner in Florida's West Melbourne, has been charged with murder after a 14-year-old boy on his bike, who was hit by Patel, died. Patel was initially arrested on October 13 after investigators found that Patel intentionally hit Hunter Russey and then left him to die. Russey was found unresponsive when cops found him. He was transferred to Orlando Health Children's Arnold Palmer Hospital with such severe injuries that he had to be put on life support.On October 17, Russey was taken off life support on his family's consent and he died. His family chose to donte his organs to help others.Patel was arrested again on October 18 and this time he was charged with second-degree murder. He is being held at the Brevard County jail without bond, local reports said. Earlier, he was charged with aggravated battery and leaving the scene of a crash involving great bodily injuryPatel suspected Russey of a break-in attempt at his shop, followed and hit himThe crash happened shortly after 4:30 am Tuesday along Cocoanut Grove Avenue. Police say Patel intentionally hit Russey, who was riding a bike, with his vehicle before taking off and leaving him to die. Patel told officers that he had spotted someone outside his store on Wickham Road after there was an alert about a possible burglary.He didn't inform law enforcement, but he started following the person. "He continues to follow him, doesn't call law enforcement, doesn't notify law enforcement that this is going on, and at some point runs into the bicyclist trying to stop him," said Lt. Graig Erenstoft, a spokesperson for the West Melbourne Police Department."During the investigation, detectives determined that Patel had intentionally struck the juvenile with his vehicle, left the scene, and returned to the store," the department said. "Patel withheld this information from responding officers and did not disclose his involvement until confronted by detectives. As a result, the juvenile remained on the side of the roadway for nearly an hour without medical assistance due to Patel failing to stop to render aid or notify Law Enforcement.""It doesn't matter what age they are. You can't chase somebody down and hit them. You just can't," Robert Mandell, a criminal defense attorney who is not connected to the case told Wesh 2 News, commenting on the case. "That's what [police are] there for. That's what insurance is for. ... You cannot take the law into your own hands and strike somebody with a deadly weapon ... and just take matters into your own hands. The law doesn't work that way."Police have not confirmed whether Russey broke into Patel's shop.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Bob Barker spent nearly $1 million to move three elephants from Toronto Zoo in 2013; Iringa, Toka and Thika arrived at a California sanctuary after a campaign to secure them a different home
articles.summary: When three ageing African elephants left Toronto Zoo in October 2013 after years of debate over their future, television host Bob Barker was waiting in
articles.body: When three ageing African elephants left Toronto Zoo in October 2013 after years of debate over their future, television host Bob Barker was waiting in California to welcome them. The former host of The Price Is Right had reportedly spent nearly $1 million to fund their journey to a sanctuary, hoping to give Iringa, Toka and Thika a different life away from their zoo enclosure. The Los Angeles Times reported on October 23, 2013, that Barker watched the elephants arrive at the Performing Animal Welfare Society's (PAWS) ARK 2000 sanctuary in San Andreas, California, visibly moved by the moment.“I had a lump in my throat, I had tears in my eyes,” Barker said at a news conference after the animals arrived, according to the Los Angeles Times. For the veteran television personality, the relocation was the culmination of a campaign that had lasted years and involved animal-welfare advocates, zoo officials and Toronto's city council.A campaign that took yearsThe decision to move the elephants was not made overnight. In May 2011, Toronto Zoo's board voted to close its elephant exhibit and relocate its remaining elephants to an appropriate facility. The move was part of a wider debate about the space and care available to elephants in captivity. Toronto City Council formally adopted a motion on October 24 and 25, 2011, directing zoo staff to arrange the transfer of Iringa, Toka and Thika to PAWS in California. The city's official records state that the sanctuary would take responsibility for arranging and paying for safe transportation, subject to permits and applicable standards.Barker was among the prominent advocates who lobbied for the move. He agreed to fund the expensive transportation after the relocation effort encountered obstacles. The amount was reported at nearly $1 million.The campaign also faced delays over the suitability of the proposed destination and the arrangements needed to move the animals safely. Toronto City Council revisited the issue in November 2012, reaffirming its decision to send the elephants to PAWS after reviewing the facility.Who were Iringa, Toka and Thika?The three elephants had spent decades at Toronto Zoo. Their histories, documented in a September 2013 update published by the zoo, show how long they had lived in human care. Iringa was born in Mozambique in 1969 and arrived at Toronto Zoo in 1974, when she was about five years old. Zoo staff described her as intelligent and sometimes unpredictable. She was also known for her fondness for younger elephants.Toka, born in Mozambique in 1970, arrived at the zoo in 1974 at the age of four. Her keepers described her as gentle and compliant. She gave birth to a calf named Toronto in 1984 and was remembered by staff as a good mother.Thika had a different distinction; she was the first African elephant born in Canada. She was born at Toronto Zoo on October 18, 1980. Staff described her as energetic, sociable and fond of interacting with other elephants.By the time of their relocation in 2013, the three animals had spent most of their lives at the zoo. Their transfer was therefore not simply a long-distance journey; it also meant adapting to an unfamiliar environment after decades in a familiar one.A nearly four-day journeyThe elephants reached PAWS' ARK 2000 sanctuary on October 20, 2013, after travelling from Toronto in a journey that took nearly four days by truck. The operation required extensive preparation. Toronto Zoo said its staff had been training the elephants for transport and coordinating with PAWS as permits and other arrangements were completed. Handlers and veterinarians accompanied the animals during the trip, the newspaper reported.The Toronto Zoo subsequently confirmed that all three elephants had arrived safely. Staff members were present as the animals were unloaded from individual steel crates. The zoo said the elephants had travelled well, eaten regularly and remained calm during the journey.For Barker, who was 89 at the time, seeing them arrive was an emotional experience. ABC News reported that he had no regrets about the money spent to make the relocation possible. The former television host had long supported animal-welfare causes and was outspoken about the treatment of animals in captivity.Barker's contribution to animal welfareBarker was best known to millions of viewers as the host of CBS' *The Price Is Right*, a role he held from 1972 until his retirement in 2007. The programme became one of American television's best-known game shows, but Barker also used his public profile to support animal-welfare causes.His funding of the elephants' relocation reflected that commitment. Speaking after their arrival, he said he had enjoyed a well-paid career and wanted to spend his money on causes he considered important.For Iringa, Toka and Thika, the journey from Toronto to California represented a major change late in their lives. For Barker and the campaigners who had pushed for the move, their arrival at PAWS was the outcome of years of advocacy, public debate and logistical planning.At ARK 2000, the elephants were expected to adjust gradually to their new surroundings. PAWS co-founder and president Ed Stewart told the Los Angeles Times that the adjustment could take weeks, months or even longer. The sanctuary intended to give each elephant the care, time and space needed to settle in. The organisation said the three would eventually share an 80-acre natural habitat with resident African elephants. PAWS also assumed responsibility for their lifelong care, distinguishing Barker's contribution to the transport from the sanctuary's ongoing financial obligations.The relocation did not instantly resolve every question about the elephants' welfare. Moving animals that have lived in a zoo for decades requires careful management, veterinary oversight and time to adapt. Nevertheless, the arrival marked the end of a prolonged effort to find them another home.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Watch: US soldier dies after falling 170 feet during fast-rope demonstration in Texas
articles.summary: A US Air Force airman died after falling around 170 feet from the ceiling of a stadium during a fast-rope demonstration ahead of a college football game
articles.body: A US Air Force airman died after falling around 170 feet from the ceiling of a stadium during a fast-rope demonstration ahead of a college football game in Texas on Saturday.The airman, identified as Tech. Sgt. Ian Patterson, was participating in a pregame demonstration at the Alamodome in San Antonio before the University of Texas at San Antonio (UTSA) Roadrunners faced the Navy Midshipmen, The New York Post reported.Patterson, a Tactical Air Control Party instructor assigned to the 6th Combat Training Squadron, Detachment 2, lost control while descending a rope during the demonstration, according to reports. He was one of four military personnel scheduled to rappel from the stadium's rafters to the field as part of UTSA's annual “Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans” event.Emergency crews rushed to Patterson's aid and provided medical assistance on the field for around 10 minutes before he was taken to a nearby hospital, where he died from his injuries.According to CBS News, Patterson had served in the Air Force for 15 years and was originally from Fort Stewart, Georgia. He was named the Air Force Special Warfare Enlisted Instructor of the Year in 2022.Crowd falls silent as demonstration turns fatalThe incident took place around 15 minutes before kickoff and brought activity on the field to a halt. According to the San Antonio Express-News, UTSA staff members formed a semicircle around Patterson before he was moved on a stretcher.Adrian Corey, a witness, told KSAT that the crowd fell silent and the stadium band stopped performing after the fall.UTSA head coach Jeff Traylor described the incident as heartbreaking, saying it had a noticeable impact on the more than 23,000 fans present at the stadium.“You could tell the energy was just gone,” Traylor said. “It just really puts things in perspective. It really does.”The incident delayed the start of the game by around 10 minutes. The match went ahead, with UTSA defeating Navy 38-34.Air Force, UTSA express condolencesThe US Air Force expressed grief over Patterson's death, with Brig. Gen. Scott C. Mills, commander of the 57th Wing, saying the loss was deeply felt across the unit.“Tech. Sgt. Patterson and his service mattered immensely to our wing, and to the family, friends, and teammates who had the privilege of knowing and serving alongside him,” Mills said.He added that the unit was focused on supporting Patterson's family, loved ones and fellow airmen. Mills also thanked the San Antonio community and mission partners at Joint Base San Antonio for their support.UTSA also expressed condolences to Patterson's family and military colleagues. The university said counselling and other support services were available to students, faculty and staff affected by the incident.The American Conference said representatives of both participating universities, Alamodome management, local authorities and other officials met with Commissioner Tim Pernetti during the game to review the available information and discuss next steps.“In accordance with conference bylaws and with the support of both participating member institutions, the conference made the decision to continue the game,” it said.The circumstances surrounding Patterson's death remain under investigation.You use AI every day. articles.title: In pictures: French landmarks damaged and destroyed by violent protesters
articles.summary: France is used to protests but the violence and damage seen across the country is shocking many people.
articles.body:
Local curfews may come into force in French towns following a weekend of disorder.

Most of the protesters were peaceful in expressing their opposition to rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.

But others - dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas - set fire to cars, shops and buildings.

The scale of the destruction - including to some iconic landmarks - has shocked many in a country used to street protests.

The damage in the capital city is extensive. Shop fronts have been broken and stores looted.

The iconic Place de la Republique was vandalised, too.

A yellow vest - representative of the movement which helped co-ordinate the weekend protests - was draped around the body of the Statue of the Republic, erected in 1883.

Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, took over parts of the capital and wreaked havoc.

Tear gas and stun grenades were fired at hundreds of people but police struggled to contain smaller groups of people roving around the city attack businesses.

The full extent of the damage did not become clear until dawn broke on Sunday.

Further south in Marseille, protesters broke into the city hall by using a metal fence as a battering ram.

A bust of Marianne - symbol of the French Republic - was damaged and knocked to the floor in Marseille as people ransacked the building.

City Mayor Benoît Payan was furious with the "almost total lack of control" by the security forces.

"The world's sixth largest power does not deserve this. The world is watching us, this morning we are the shame of Europe," he said.

In the city of Lyon, Mayor Grégory Doucet said the burning of the city's tourist office, housed in a 19th Century building, was "a tragedy".

Fire crews also battled a fire at Limoges town hall, which caused part of the building to collapse. Local officials said the town hall was "largely lost".

"A wild horde" had "deliberately" set fire to the 143-year-old building, said Maurice Barate, the prefect for the Haute-Vienne department.

French authorities have admitted they lost control of cities to the protesters.

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez offered his resignation - which has been rejected.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has given local mayors the power to introduce partial curfews in some parts of the country, which he says is designed to protect people and businesses.

But the French are holding their breath - in anticipation of another chapter in this protest next Saturday.

articles.title: US National Guard member shot in leg during fight in Washington DC; suspect wounded in gunfire exchange
articles.summary: A US National Guard member was shot in the leg while trying to break up a fight in Washington, DC, on Sunday night.
articles.body: A US National Guard member was shot in the leg while trying to break up a fight in Washington, DC, on Sunday night. The suspected shooter was also wounded in an exchange of gunfire with Guard members, police said Monday.The incident took place around 11.10 pm on Sunday in the Eastern Market neighbourhood of southeast Washington, when seven or eight National Guard members stationed in a parked van heard a fight unfolding on a sidewalk.The Guard members got out of the vehicle to intervene when a person involved in the altercation pulled out a gun and began firing, interim Metropolitan Police Department chief Jeffery Carroll told reporters.The suspect then ran into an alley, where Guard members ordered the person to drop the weapon. However, the individual pointed the gun towards the service members, prompting them to return fire, Carroll said.One National Guard member was struck in the leg, while the suspect was shot in the abdomen. Both were taken to hospitals with injuries that were not considered life-threatening, police said.Three Guard members fired their weapons during the encounter. The suspect was arrested, and the police department is investigating the shooting.Carroll said there was no further threat to the community and urged anyone with information about the incident to contact the police.Trump's National Guard deployment in WashingtonUS President Donald Trump deployed the National Guard to Washington in August 2025 as part of a crime-fighting initiative. The force, which reached around 5,000 troops at its peak over the summer, has supported arrests, patrolled neighbourhoods and participated in city clean-up efforts.The Republican administration has credited the deployment with helping reduce crime in the capital. However, crime had already been declining before the Guard arrived.Officials, activists and residents in the predominantly Democratic city have criticised the deployment, arguing that it wastes taxpayer money and normalises the militarisation of an American city.You use AI every day. articles.title: Manipur violence: CM condemns killing of three civilians, orders tighter security in vulnerable areas
articles.summary: Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh on Monday condemned the killing of three civilians by suspected militants in the border area of Imphal East and
articles.body: Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh on Monday condemned the killing of three civilians by suspected militants in the border area of Imphal East and Kangpokpi districts and directed officials to strengthen security in vulnerable areas of the state.The three victims were among a group of Meitei villagers collecting firewood in a forest when unidentified gunmen opened fire on them, officials said.Three others were injured and three people were reported missing.The attack triggered protests in Imphal, where demonstrators placed two bodies outside the chief minister's residence. Police fired tear gas shells to disperse the protesters.Singh chaired a security review meeting attended by home minister Govindas Konthoujam, chief secretary Rajeev Singh Thakur, security advisor Kuldiep Singh, director general of police Mukesh Singh and senior officers from the Army, Assam Rifles, CRPF, BSF and other security agencies.An official statement said the meeting reviewed the state's overall security situation and discussed the previous day's incident in Thoubal district and the latest attack in Imphal East.The chief minister “strongly condemned the killing of innocent civilians by armed miscreants at Nongshum in Imphal East district”, the statement said.Combing operation launched, helicopters deployedSecurity forces launched a combing operation in the Sunurok hills of Kangpokpi district following the attack, deploying sniffer dogs and drones to search the area. Helicopters were also being used for surveillance, news agency ANI reported.Additional director general of police (law and order) Lhari Dorjee Lhatoo said unidentified militants opened fire at around 9.40 am on a group of villagers cutting and transporting firewood near Sunurok hills under Sagolmang police station.“Three individuals died in the incident while three more sustained injuries and they are now under medical care,” Lhatoo said.A joint team comprising police, CRPF, CoBRA, Assam Rifles and BSF personnel was conducting the operation, he added. Mobile checkposts had also been established, while security agencies were closely monitoring the situation.“Police, in close coordination with CRPF, BSF, Army, Assam Rifles and other sister security agencies, is working continuously to maintain law and order, and to prevent further escalation,” Lhatoo said.He assured the public that strict action would be taken against those responsible and appealed to people to exercise restraint.Singh later visited the injured at a private hospital and assured them that the state government would cover their medical expenses.NDA MLAs condemn killingsThe chief minister subsequently chaired a meeting of National Democratic Alliance (NDA) legislators at the chief minister's Secretariat.In a social media post, Singh said the legislators had unanimously condemned the killings and demanded the immediate arrest of those responsible.“The legislators unanimously condemned the killings of three civilians in the strongest terms. They demanded that police and security forces apprehend the perpetrators of the crime immediately,” he said.Protests also erupted at Khwairamband Ima market in Imphal following the attack, with heavy security deployed in the area.Fresh violence follows deadly clash in ThoubalThe killings came a day after violence in Manipur's Thoubal district left one person dead and several others injured in clashes between two communities.The confrontation reportedly took place during a musical programme at Cherapur in Khangabok.District authorities imposed prohibitory orders in the affected areas, restricting residents from leaving their homes. A few houses and vehicles were also set on fire.The deceased was identified as Laishram Rakesh Singh, who was reportedly struck by a stone during the clashes. Villagers subsequently blocked National Highway 2, demanding justice and action against those involved in his death.In a separate social media post, Singh said he had met representatives of a Joint Action Committee formed over Rakesh's killing.The committee submitted a memorandum raising concerns about the case, and the chief minister assured its members that their demands would be examined and appropriate action taken under the law.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Khosla ka Ghosla: Silicon Valley superstar is hiring chief of staff, expect no rest in the nest
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: Vinod Khosla has spent decades in Silicon Valley funding companies and entrepreneurs who overturn conventional wisdom,
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: Vinod Khosla has spent decades in Silicon Valley funding companies and entrepreneurs who overturn conventional wisdom, disrupt industries, and remake the future. His latest quest, for an aide who doesn’t need downtime, is rather more prosaic, but has still prompted furious workplace debates.The 71-year-old co-founder of Sun Microsystems and boss of Khosla Ventures last week sought a chief of staff with a social media post that left the tech world in a tizzy.He offered a front-row seat to some of the most consequential technology bets in the world with a job description that some said resembled a three-year surrender agreement, involving 12-hour workdays and giving up any lingering attachment to weekends.The successful candidate is expected to work in person in Menlo Park, California, generally from 8 am to 8 pm, while maintaining “around-the-clock availability, including nights and weekends when needed.”The salary? Not disclosed. The job involves evaluating investments, meeting founders, researching emerging technologies and helping Khosla's portfolio companies. Expectations from applicants include “integrity, composure, and low ego.”In return, they get the chance to learn from a guru whose early bets include OpenAI, DoorDash and Instacart.The advertisement quickly became a referendum on Silicon Valley’s favourite workplace religion: the belief that extraordinary success requires extraordinary hours, echoing a similar call made some years ago by Infosys’ NR Narayan Murthy, who suggested a 70-hour workweek for Indian youth.“Your work-life balance need not apply” and “say good-bye to wife and kids” were some of the jokes that bounced around social media.Khosla, who has never been accused of being short on opinions, stepped in to clarify matters. “Jokes aside honest truth is this job has no specific hours requirement but is intense. I work 80 hours/week and this person needs to keep up. Doing, learning & more.... and very fun,” he said in a follow-up post.While trolls trashed the prospect of a tortured existence, joking that the phrase “I’m just heading out” might qualify as grounds for firing, some prominent tech figures saw a career-making opportunity.Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian endorsed the role as one that could change a person’s life, while Matteo Franceschetti, founder of sleep-technology company Eight Sleep, said he would take it himself if he were not busy running his own company, prompting Khosla to tell him, “As one of our portfolio entrepreneurs, I prefer you build Eight Sleep!”Born in Pune, India, Khosla studied at IIT Delhi before earning degrees at Carnegie Mellon University and Stanford Graduate School of Business.He co-founded Sun Microsystems in 1982, helping build one of the defining companies of the early internet era, before establishing Khosla Ventures in 2004.Today, his firm invests across AI, software, healthcare, energy and climate technology and has built a reputation for backing unconventional ideas early, betting on technologies that established investors might consider too risky.He is also known for blunt, sometimes abrasive interventions in public debates. In June, he excoriated Stanford students who protested Google CEO Sundar Pichai during a commencement address, describing their actions as “biased, idiotic, short-sighted and very selfish.”The students were objecting to Google’s contracts and links to the Israeli government and US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).It is this combination- visionary investor, relentless operator and unapologetically combative personality- that makes the chief-of-staff opening so intriguing. “It is intense, always on, fun, never boring, but fulfilling/ rewarding.Not for the faint of heart, not for your average person, not the average VC, but for someone who wants to take on a lot + a ton of responsibility to do and build awesome things in the world with someone who has a relentless mission,” pitched in Kristina Simmons, a former Khosla aide who is now a Founder and Managing Partner of Overwater Ventures, an early-stage VC firm.So for all the jokes about forfeiting weekends and surrendering to the 80-hour week, Khosla’s pitch boils down to a quintessential Silicon Valley bargain: trade a chunk of your life for a crash course in how the future is financed.Whether that sounds like a dream job or an endurance test may depend on one’s appetite for ambition -- and how much sleep one is willing to sacrifice for it.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2023, a visitor dropped a Cheetos bag in Carlsbad Caverns’ Big Room in New Mexico; it triggered fungal growth, attracted insects and spiders, and disrupted the fragile ecosystem
articles.summary: A seemingly harmless snack can have unexpected consequences for the natural world.
articles.body: A seemingly harmless snack can have unexpected consequences for the natural world. In the summer of 2023, a visitor dropped a bag of Cheetos inside Carlsbad Caverns National Park in southeastern New Mexico, inadvertently disturbing the delicate ecosystem of one of its caves.The incident took place in the Big Room, an enormous underground chamber known for its striking stalactites and stalagmites. While the discarded snack bag might have appeared insignificant to a visitor, it created conditions that encouraged microbial growth and attracted other organisms, prompting park rangers to intervene.According to the National Park Service (NPS), the incident demonstrated how even small amounts of foreign material can have an outsized impact on an isolated natural environment.How a discarded Cheetos bag disrupted the cave ecosystemThe cave’s high humidity played a crucial role in what happened next. The processed corn in the Cheetos softened in the damp conditions, providing a source of nutrients for fungi and microbes.In a Facebook post describing the incident, the National Park Service explained that the snack residue created an environment in which microbial life and fungi could thrive. Cave crickets, mites, spiders and flies subsequently gathered around the area, forming a temporary food web as nutrients spread into the surrounding cave environment.The NPS also noted that mould spread across nearby surfaces before the organisms eventually died and decomposed, continuing the cycle of nutrient transfer.The incident illustrates how introducing food into an environment that is largely isolated from the outside world can alter the natural balance, even when the amount of material involved is relatively small.Why the cave’s high humidity made a differenceCarlsbad Caverns’ humid conditions helped the snack residue break down and supported the growth of fungi and mould.Speaking to National Geographic at the time, park guide Ashley Parsons explained that humidity levels inside the cave typically range from 90 to 100 per cent, allowing the discarded food to become soggy quickly.Joseph C. Ward of the National Park Service also described the consequences in an interview with KCRW in November 2024. He explained that fungi and mould began growing around the site where the bag had landed, attracting other life forms, including mites, springtails and cave spiders.How park rangers cleaned up the Cheetos spillAfter discovering the discarded bag and the growth around it, park rangers assessed how best to remove the material without causing further damage to the cave.They collected nearly all the spilled snack material and used a toothbrush to remove the rings of mould and fungi that had developed around the affected area.According to the account shared by the National Park Service, the cleanup took approximately 20 minutes.The National Park Service used the episode to remind visitors that their actions can have consequences far beyond what they can immediately see.The agency acknowledged that some impacts of tourism are difficult to avoid, such as the tiny fibres of lint left behind by people walking through a cave. However, it stressed that other forms of damage, including dropping food or leaving litter behind, are entirely preventable.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 2 years of protests, one crucial election: Serbia's students challenge Vucic's 14-year rule
articles.summary: Serbia’s student-led anti-corruption movement, which emerged after a deadly railway station disaster in November 2024, is now mounting its biggest
articles.body: Serbia’s student-led anti-corruption movement, which emerged after a deadly railway station disaster in November 2024, is now mounting its biggest political challenge yet to populist leader Aleksandar Vucic, with an early parliamentary election on October 25 threatening to end the ruling party’s 14-year grip on power.The election comes amid heightened tensions over alleged surveillance and intimidation of government critics. On Monday, digital rights researchers said they had confirmed with “high confidence” that the phone of Vladan Djokic, rector of the University of Belgrade and a prominent supporter of the protests, was infected with Pegasus spyware in 2026 reported AP.The Citizen Lab research group said it conducted the forensic analysis in cooperation with Serbia-based digital rights organisation SHARE Foundation. Pegasus, developed by Israeli company NSO Group, can infiltrate smartphones and give operators access to messages, location data, microphones and cameras.The findings follow reports in September that at least 14 activists and students had their phones hacked and infected with spyware, including Pegasus. Serbian authorities have previously denied involvement in such attacks. There was no immediate comment from the authorities on the latest findings.Djokic described the alleged hacking as a “serious attack on my privacy, security and the integrity of the post of rector”. He added that it was “yet another attempt of intimidation designed to prevent any critical position and public action”.The allegations have added to concerns over the treatment of government critics as the student movement prepares for a decisive electoral contest against Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party (SNS).How did the protests begin?The protests first started in November 2024 after a concrete canopy at a railway station in Novi Sad, Serbia’s second-largest city, collapsed, killing 16 people.The tragedy triggered widespread anger over alleged corruption and negligence in public infrastructure projects. Students demanded accountability for the deaths, arguing that corruption and failures in oversight had contributed to the disaster.What began as a demand for justice soon grew into a nationwide movement against corruption and the government’s handling of public institutions. University students organised demonstrations, blocked faculties and mobilised supporters across the country.The protests put growing pressure on Vucic’s government and contributed to a political crisis that forced a government collapse. Students have since emerged as a significant political force, challenging a ruling party that has dominated Serbian politics for 14 years.Psychology professor Aleksandar Baucal, an early supporter of the movement who is now on the students’ election ticket, said the protests reflected a broader frustration with the state of Serbian society.“Their generation grew up in a society that is deeply unjust,” Baucal said. “They realised that if they gave up, they would give up on their lives,” he added. “This has made them an opponent who can't give up.”The student movement has now evolved from a protest campaign into an electoral challenge, seeking to translate public anger over corruption into political change.The early parliamentary election on October 25 pits Vucic’s SNS against a student-backed electoral ticket known as the Students’ List. The 250-seat parliament is at the centre of the contest, with the outcome expected to determine whether the ruling party can extend its hold on power.Vucic resigned as president last month to pursue a return as prime minister, according to the Associated Press report. The veteran politician has repeatedly accused the student protests of being organised from abroad to “destroy” the country, without providing evidence for the claims.The students, meanwhile, say their objective extends beyond replacing the government. They want to rebuild democratic institutions, tackle corruption and strengthen independent media to create conditions for free and fair elections in the future.Their candidates were selected through a process involving proposals and vetting at universities across Serbia. The list includes teachers, professors, experts, athletes, farmers and artists, alongside more familiar public figures.Vukasin Djinovic, a student from Novi Sad, said the movement’s collective approach set it apart from the country's established political leadership.“It has been important for us to dismantle the personality cult,” he told the Associated Press.The movement has no single leader or spokesperson. Instead, students say decisions are taken collectively through faculty assemblies, known as plenums, where participants discuss and vote on plans.Djinovic said the movement supports “democracy, tolerance and respect for everyone's opinion”.The approach has helped the students present themselves as an alternative to Vucic’s centralised political leadership, although the election will test whether their protest support can translate into votes.Surveillance allegations and fears of a crackdownThe campaign is unfolding amid accusations of surveillance, detentions and pressure on government opponents.The student movement warned on Sunday that its meetings were being monitored and alleged that authorities planned to detain some of its members ahead of a major rally scheduled for Thursday. Police had not commented on the allegations.Several students have been detained during the protests on accusations including anti-state activities. The authorities’ actions have drawn criticism from demonstrators, who say pressure has strengthened rather than weakened their movement.The Pegasus findings have brought renewed attention to the risks faced by activists and public figures critical of the government. SHARE Foundation warned that, without an effective investigation and accountability, “there is a serious risk that digital repression will continue and spread further, reaching every part of society and every critical voice”.A separate analysis is also under way to establish whether the phone of associate prosecutor Rade Bajic was hacked. Bajic worked on a corruption case linked to a proposed luxury development at a former military compound bombed during the 1999 NATO campaign. The project was linked to a company associated with Jared Kushner, US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, and was later cancelled.Bajic was replaced after speaking out about the alleged corruption. A government minister and several others charged in the case are on trial in Serbia.NSO Group says it sells its technology to government agencies to combat serious crime and terrorism. However, investigations by journalists and human rights researchers have documented its use against journalists, activists and other members of civil society. The US Commerce Department placed the company on its trade blacklist in November 2021, citing evidence that foreign governments had used its spyware to target journalists, activists and government officials.What is at stake in the election?The October 25 vote is being watched closely because it could determine whether the student movement can turn nearly two years of demonstrations into a direct challenge to the ruling establishment.The SNS and the Students’ List are believed to be running close, according to the Associated Press, making the result uncertain. International election monitors and the European Union have raised concerns about the safety and fairness of the vote.The ruling party has faced previous accusations of election irregularities, including voter pressure, bribery and inflated voter lists. The party has denied the allegations.Analysts fear that both sides could claim victory on election night and that a defeat for the ruling party could trigger further confrontation.Political scientist Aleksandra Krstic, from Belgrade’s Faculty of Political Sciences, said the students had given people hope that political change was possible.“Students have shown clearly that they are the force, both as a generation and politically, that can bring about a change,” she said.“That is what gave people hope, that it can be different after 14 years of the Serbian Progressive Party regime,” Krstic added.But she warned that tensions remained high: “We all fear extreme violence.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Meet Sasha Bogosian, the 18-year-old Los Angeles student who started painting jeans while recovering from leg surgery at 8; a decade later, her nonprofit has raised nearly $100,000 for children's hospital art therapy
articles.summary: An 18-year-old student from Los Angeles who began painting denim while recovering from major bone surgery at the age of eight has raised nearly $100,000
articles.body: An 18-year-old student from Los Angeles who began painting denim while recovering from major bone surgery at the age of eight has raised nearly $100,000 for art programmes at children's hospitals. Sasha Bogosian was born with cerebral palsy right hemiplegia, a neurological condition that affects movement and strength on the right side of her body. She developed the condition after suffering a stroke during childbirth. In 2016, after undergoing major surgery on her leg and hips, Bogosian began painting denim jeans and jackets as part of her recovery at home. The activity helped her rebuild motor skills in her hands. What began as a quiet creative hobby soon grew into The Sasha Project LA, a registered non-profit organisation that raises money for creative therapy programmes for children who spend long periods in hospital.Turning medical recovery into creative actionDuring her early recovery at home, Bogosian looked for ways to keep her hands active despite her physical limitations. Using acrylic paint, she began creating colourful splatter-art designs on denim clothes given to her by friends and family. According to background information published on The Sasha Project LA website, Bogosian became a Junior Ambassador for Children's Hospital Los Angeles (CHLA) in 2016, when she was eight years old. She found that creative therapy helped her cope with physical pain and anxiety. That same year, she started her non-profit organisation to raise money directly for art programmes in hospitals. "Sasha is soft-spoken, but her painted jeans speak volumes," reads the organisation's official description. "What started as a fun craft and form of art therapy soon became something much bigger, a way to give back." The money raised by her non-profit supports The Mark Taper-Johnny Mercer Artists Program at Children's Hospital Los Angeles. The programme brings visual artists, musicians, and performers to patients' bedsides. These activities help children express feelings of grief, frustration, or fear while receiving treatment.Clinical benefits and insurance gapsCreative therapies have recognised benefits in children's healthcare, but hospitals continue to face challenges in paying for these services. Information published by CHLA and shared on The Sasha Project LA platform explains that expressive art therapies can provide measurable health benefits. These include lower blood pressure, better breathing control, pain relief, and improved motor skills as children grow and develop. However, expressive arts programmes are considered an additional form of care, so standard health insurance policies in the United States do not cover their running costs. As a result, hospital art therapy departments depend entirely on charitable donations and independent fundraising to continue their work. Along with individual art sessions at patients' bedsides, donations raised through Bogosian's project help fund the Handy Heroes Therapy Camp. This specialised summer day camp is designed for children with hemiparesis, a condition that causes weakness on one side of the body. It offers tailored physical therapy and group activities to help strengthen affected limbs.Runway showcases and corporate partnershipsAs Bogosian's hand-painted denim designs attracted more public attention, major clothing and footwear brands began supporting her fundraising work. Retailers such as Levi's and BLICK Art Materials started sponsoring her workspace by providing plain denim and professional art supplies. In 2018, Bogosian was chosen as one of ten National Champion Ambassadors representing Children's Miracle Network Hospitals across North America. During her time in the role, she led a fundraising fashion show called "Rock the Runway." Other young patients modelled her custom hand-painted denim designs alongside celebrity supporters. Bogosian has also expanded her work into accessible fashion. She partnered with Billy Footwear to release collections of adaptive shoes designed for people who wear leg braces or have limited mobility. After undergoing a second major surgery in 2019 to manage her condition, Bogosian continued her physical rehabilitation while studying fashion design.Expansion into adaptive fashionNow 18, Bogosian is studying adaptive clothing design. She plans to launch a fully inclusive fashion brand designed for people with physical disabilities. Outside her studies and charity work, Bogosian stays active through targeted fitness training and pickleball. She continues her physical therapy routine while organising seasonal fundraising campaigns. So far, money raised through custom clothing sales, corporate partnerships, and direct public donations through The Sasha Project LA website continues to go directly to Children's Hospital Los Angeles. The funds help support full-time art therapists employed by the hospital.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Hours after custody extension, Delhi Police transfers CJP leaders' trespassing case to crime branch
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Monday transferred the trespassing case against Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das to the crime
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Monday transferred the trespassing case against Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das to the crime branch, news agency ANI reported, citing sources.This came hours after a Delhi court extended the CJP leaders' judicial custody by two days for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar, which is no longer a designated protest venue, and obstructing police personnel on duty.Along with other CJP workers, they waved the national flag at the site and raised slogans against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar before being detained and placed under preventive custody.According to their lawyer, their bail sureties were rejected due to a reported mismatch in documents. They will now be produced before the court on Wednesday."Today, when we reached the court, the five-day custody period had ended. On the last date of hearing, the court had stated that it did not find the sureties legitimate enough to be accepted. Today, we produced fresh sureties and brought them to court. When our matter was taken up, the State filed a fresh application, which was served on us at that point. In this application, they sought a further five to seven days of judicial custody," the CJP leaders' advocate said."The reasons they gave were absolutely shocking to us. They claimed there was an imminent threat to public order and public tranquillity and that, therefore, the accused needed to remain in judicial custody... It is very unfortunate, and everyone must remember that there is currently no FIR against my clients in connection with this issue. This concerns preventive custody. They have been detained out of fear that they might go and protest. There is no FIR, no pending case against them in this matter, and no investigation for which they need to be questioned. This is absolutely appalling and deeply disturbing. I cannot remember the last time people were kept in preventive custody under such circumstances. We will pursue the matter legally, but this has been hugely disappointing for all of us," he added.The development came amid allegations by the CJP that the bail proceedings had been deliberately delayed to prevent the release of its two convenors, who were sent to five-day judicial custody on October 13 following a protest at Jantar Mantar.On Sunday, the special executive magistrate hearing their bail matter claimed that unknown persons were threatening him, following which the police registered a non-cognisable report.Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership and praised Das and Ranka for remaining defiant despite spending five days in judicial custody."You must be feeling very strong keeping a 26-year-old Saurav Das in jail. You must be feeling very strong beating children on the streets. You must be feeling very strong putting up barricades across Delhi and dragging students on the streets," he said.Dipke claimed that Das and Ranka had gone to Jantar Mantar to wave the national flag but were sent to judicial custody. He also alleged that their court hearings had been repeatedly postponed. "Is this strength? Hiding behind the police, hiding behind the courts, is this Narendra Modi's strength?" he asked.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Two Indiana business partners agreed to split commissions from retirement seminars in 2019 without a written contract; after a money dispute, an October 15 appeals court upheld a $119,779 judgment against one partner
articles.summary: An oral business deal struck over financial seminars without a written contract has resulted in a $119,779 (£92,000) court judgment upheld by the Court of
articles.body: An oral business deal struck over financial seminars without a written contract has resulted in a $119,779 (£92,000) court judgment upheld by the Court of Appeals of Indiana. In an opinion issued on October 15, a three-judge appellate panel affirmed a trial court ruling requiring Stephen Dissette to pay damages to his former business partner, Brandon Rudd, following a dispute over split commissions generated from retirement education events. The case, Stephen Dissette v. Brandon Rudd, stemmed from an informal arrangement established in 2019. The two financial professionals agreed to co-host and present educational seminars aimed at individuals planning for retirement, with an understanding that commissions and revenues earned from client referrals would be divided between them.Informal arrangement leads to financial disputeAccording to appellate court records published by Justia Law, Dissette and Rudd began collaborating on retirement planning seminars to generate prospective wealth management clients. Under their unwritten agreement, the partners planned to share the financial rewards resulting from business leads produced by the seminars. However, after revenue began flowing in from clients recruited during the events, a disagreement emerged over the precise calculation and distribution of commission payments. Because the business partners had relied entirely on an oral arrangement rather than executing a formal written contract, the relationship deteriorated into litigation over unpaid earnings. Rudd subsequently filed a lawsuit in Indiana state court alleging breach of contract and seeking his portion of the withheld seminar commissions. Following a trial evaluating bank records, client transactions, and witness testimony, the trial court ruled in Rudd's favour and entered a judgment totaling $119,779 against Dissette.Legal principles governing unwritten contractsOn appeal to the Court of Appeals of Indiana under docket number 25A-PL-02468, Dissette challenged the trial court's decision, disputing the enforceability of the verbal agreement and the calculation of the monetary award. Under Indiana contract law, oral agreements are legally binding provided the parties demonstrate mutual assent to essential terms and exchange sufficient legal consideration. When disputes arise over unwritten contracts, trial judges serve as the primary triers of fact, tasked with evaluating witness credibility and weighing circumstantial evidence to determine the terms of the original bargain. Reviewing the lower court's findings, the Court of Appeals of Indiana determined that the trial record contained sufficient evidence demonstrating that an enforceable oral contract existed between Dissette and Rudd to split the seminar commissions. The appellate panel concluded that the trial court did not commit clear error in calculating the $119,779 judgment based on the evidence presented regarding seminar leads, client conversions, and generated commission fees.Appellate decision and final rulingWriting for the court, the appellate panel affirmed the trial court's judgment in full, rejecting Dissette's claims on appeal and leaving the $119,779 award intact. Official court records indicate the decision was handed down on October 15, 2026, conclusively resolving the legal challenge regarding the 2019 retirement seminar commissions.You use AI every day.
